summary.headline: KSB guides EBITDA at 13-14% and says fixed-price cost pressure eases by Q1 FY28, while nuclear NPCIL tender turns competitive.
summary.overview: Management at the institutional investor meet (17 Nov 2026, Q2 FY27 context) said margins are under pressure from commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts, with Valves EBIT margin cited at 2.9% by an analyst. Nine-month revenue was stated as ₹20,647 million, and YTD September orders on hand were ₹28,599 million per the slides, while Q&A referred to ₹2,600-2,800 crore order book including nuclear. Management expects price recovery in standard business over 6-9 months and says cost pressure could last at most until Q1 FY28. Nuclear: first reactor coolant pump testing has teething problems, and the 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27; the new NPCIL tender (about 32 pumps, roughly ₹4,000 crore across three sites) is now competitive with relaxed qualification.

financial_highlights.metric: ROCE excluding labour code one-time impact (last year)
Valves segment EBIT margin (per analyst question)

segments.name: Valves
segments.commentary: EBIT margin cited at 2.9% by analyst; management attributes compression to product mix shifting to project orders and commodity costs, with no volume leverage this year.

segments.name: Pumps - Standard and project business
segments.commentary: Price increases in standard business take 6-9 months to recover; project business waits for the next contract. Management said the cost squeeze should be over by Q1 FY28 at the latest.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Two pumps delivered to NPCIL, testing ongoing with teething issues; first 500-hour test may not finish in FY27. Motors and some casings invoiced, but motors are traded at low margin. Management targets up to four pumps next year.

segments.name: SupremeServ (aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Revenue growing about 12-15%; pure spares and service are roughly 12-13% of total revenue, excluding replacement pumps.

segments.name: Water and building services
segments.commentary: Targeting minimum 15%, possibly 20%, YoY growth in water/wastewater and commercial building services; new entrant in water projects, targeting 5-7% share in 3-5 years.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains EBITDA target of 13-14% and says it will not go to 15-16% as it enters new segments with lower initial margins.
Expects margin recovery via aftermarket, exports and volume; says cost pressure on fixed-price contracts should last at most to Q1 FY28.
Expects KUSUM 2.0 solar tender to start early next year after MNRE specifications are finalised next month.
Dangote refinery boiler feed pump orders of similar size to the fertiliser project (about ₹218 crore) expected to materialise this month, per management hope.
S/4HANA ERP go-live planned for February; foundry gas supply now about 85-90% back to normal.
capex_capacity: Nuclear reactor coolant pump: first pump 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27; final test leg targeted to start December and finish in the first quarter of next year.
Foundry (Vambori) gas supply disruption largely resolved; management says it is 85-90% back to earlier levels.
Shirwal energy pump factory and Shirwal expansion referenced in company history slides; no capex amount disclosed.
Mining entry supported by a newly qualified in-house foundry for exports.
demand_pricing: Order intake growing: Dangote fertiliser boiler feed pump order about ₹100 crore plus ₹118 crore; ONGC offshore pumps about ₹850 million (₹85 crore).

Supercritical thermal: JSW Salboni boiler feed pump order near finalisation; further L&T, Adani and BHEL/DVC boiler circulation pump opportunities. Management targets roughly 50% share in boiler feed pumps against Sulzer.

Nuclear NPCIL tender for about 32 reactor coolant pumps (around ₹4,000 crore across three sites) is now competitive with KSB, Kirloskar Brothers and Flowserve; qualification criteria relaxed; pre-bid meeting held next day.
Competitive intensity in India described as fierce; management says it expects to hold EBITDA margins and defend price in standard business.
Market share about 10-11% of an estimated ₹28,000-30,000 crore pump market; leader in energy, top two in industry.

qa_highlights.question: Chances and share in the new NPCIL reactor coolant pump tender, and whether margins will be lower.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on pricing or margins because specifications and commercial terms have changed; it sees competitive bidding and believes KSB's chances are good as a proven supplier.

qa_highlights.question: Why Valves EBIT margin fell to 2.9%, and how price increases will be passed on.
qa_highlights.answer: Product mix shifted toward project orders and commodity costs hit margins; standard business price increases take 6-9 months to recover; management expects a return to normal levels with higher volume and better mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~₹2,400 crore order book is fixed-price and until when margin pressure lasts.
qa_highlights.answer: All non-nuclear orders are fixed-price; management expects cost pressure at most until Q1 FY28, passing through price increases in steps to smaller suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: Testing status of nuclear pumps and whether FY guidance of two to three pumps holds.
qa_highlights.answer: Testing has teething issues in control valves, thermowell and power cable; a further two weeks is needed; the first pump's 500-hour test may slip past FY27; next year could see more than two pumps, with a target of four.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity versus Kirloskar Brothers, which reported margin expansion and share gains.
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the Indian market remains fiercely competitive; margins will be defended through aftermarket and exports, with EBITDA target kept at 13-14%.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and segment growth targets.
qa_highlights.answer: Overall share 10-11%; leads energy, top two in industry, top three to five in building services, mining and petrochemical. Targets at least 15%, possibly 20%, growth in water and building services, and growth above market in energy and industry.

risks_watch: Valves and pumps margin compression from commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts; recovery timing (Q1 FY28 at latest per management).
NPCIL nuclear testing delays and possible margin dilution in the new competitive tender; nuclear receivables and working capital.
Solar pump business slowdown for six to nine months awaiting KUSUM 2.0; management caps solar at about 10% of revenue for working capital reasons.
S/4HANA go-live in February could create process disruption; watch for execution issues.
Order intake breakup not disclosed in detail; nuclear vs non-nuclear order book split not provided numerically.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term order intake and thermal, data centre and export growth, but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, nuclear pricing and testing timelines, repeatedly saying it is too early to comment.
key_quotes: So that's why I'm not commenting too much on that.
So we, for sure know what our costs are, and we are confident that we should get a share out of this business.
So that way, we want to continue to maintain an EBITDA level of 13% to 14%. This is our goal.

adds.what: Nuclear reactor coolant pump testing (two pumps delivered to NPCIL; no new capacity disclosed)

growth.why: Management holds EBITDA margin at 13-14% and guides water and building services to minimum 15% (possibly 20%) YoY growth, backed by named orders (Dangote about ₹218 crore, ONGC about ₹85 crore, JSW Salboni near finalisation) but no new capacity, and the brief gives no quarterly revenue or EBITDA growth figure.

quality.why: The brief gives only multi-year CAGRs and a nine-month revenue figure with no YoY growth rate for Q2 FY27, and it names no driver or one-off for this quarter, so the quality of this quarter's growth cannot be judged from it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA target held at 13-14% with no move to 15-16%; Valves EBIT margin cited at 2.9%, and fixed-price cost pressure is expected to last at most until Q1 FY28, with standard-business price increases taking 6-9 months to recover.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant or line is firmly dated; nuclear pump output is tied to testing that may slip past FY27, and utilisation is only given as foundry gas supply back at 85-90%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order intake is growing (Dangote boiler feed pump about ₹218 crore, ONGC about ₹85 crore, JSW Salboni near finalisation) and water/building services is targeted at minimum 15%, possibly 20%, YoY growth, though no quarterly volume figure was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond the Shirwal references with no amount disclosed, and utilisation was not quoted as a percentage.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 13-14% EBITDA target and called the nuclear tender pricing too early to comment, with competitive bidding and a fierce Indian market.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Nuclear 500-hour test may slip beyond FY27 and the NPCIL tender (about 32 pumps, roughly ₹4,000 crore) is now competitive with relaxed qualification, so margin dilution is a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is entering water projects (targeting 5-7% share in 3-5 years) and mining via a newly qualified in-house foundry for exports, but no dated product launch was given.

rows.label: NPCIL reactor coolant pump tender (~32 pumps, ~₹4,000 crore)
rows.why: The tender is now competitive with KSB, Kirloskar Brothers and Flowserve, and management believes its chances are good as a proven supplier, but pricing is unresolved and the nuclear pump test may slip.

rows.label: Standard-business price recovery
rows.why: Management expects price increases in standard business to recover in 6-9 months, and cost pressure on fixed-price contracts to last at most until Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Exports at 15-20% of revenue
rows.why: Management targets exports at 15-20% of revenue and cites exports as a margin-recovery lever, with exports growing 22% CAGR per slides, though no quarterly export figure was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term order intake, thermal and exports but cautious and evasive on near-term margins, nuclear pricing and testing timelines; analysts pressed on the Valves EBIT margin falling to 2.9% and on nuclear tender pricing.
